builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: VenusRL: A Fully Disaggregated Agentic RL System with Priority Scheduling and Scalable Interaction
summary: VenusRL replaces static per-group rollout scheduling and statically over-provisioned tool sandboxes with priority-aware scheduling (based on length prediction) and a template-keyed page-sharing pool with copy-on-write isolation. The cost is substantial systems complexity: a fully disaggregated architecture spanning batch admission, KV cache residency, and cross-worker orchestration, plus OS-level page-table aliasing, which assumes a multi-node RL training cluster. Failure modes include mispredicted trajectory lengths starving groups, page-sharing bugs breaking memory isolation between sandboxes, and gains evaporating at small rollout scale where straggler effects are minor.
rationale: The technique targets multi-node, multi-GPU agentic RL training at a scale far beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-based setup, so the reader has no infrastructure on which to deploy it.
technique: Disaggregated agentic RL scheduling and sandbox sharing

The cost is substantial systems complexity: a fully disaggregated architecture spanning batch admission, KV cache residency, and cross-worker orchestration, plus OS-level page-table aliasing, which assumes a multi-node RL training cluster. Failure modes include mispredicted trajectory lengths starving groups, page-sharing bugs breaking memory isolation between sandboxes, and gains evaporating at small rollout scale where straggler effects are minor.
Up to 4.24x end-to-end training speedup over state-of-the-art agentic RL baselines and up to 89% reduction in environment cost.
